    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "NumStability.leveque01Equation11RiemannData",
      "interpretation": "An abbreviation applying IsRiemannData to a real-position function valued in Fin m → Real and two states.",
      "effect_on_target": "The left side of the equivalence expands directly to the two open-half-line conditions in D003.",
      "source_match": "Matches Equation (1.11) using initialState x for q(x,0).",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "NumStability.riemannData",
      "interpretation": "Returns leftState when x < 0, rightState when 0 < x, and valueAtOrigin otherwise.",
      "effect_on_target": "Constructs a total initial function; real-order trichotomy confines its third branch to zero. The target existentially quantifies that branch's value.",
      "source_match": "The two prescribed branches match (1.11); existential quantification leaves the unprescribed interface value unrestricted.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "NumStability.IsRiemannData",
      "interpretation": "The conjunction of data x = leftState for every negative real x and data x = rightState for every positive real x.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the entire initial-data predicate without a condition at zero or an evolution equation.",
      "source_match": "Exactly reproduces the displayed branch prescription in (1.11).",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "Eq",
      "interpretation": "Lean's homogeneous propositional equality.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses exact state equality in D003 and equality of total functions in the existential characterization.",
      "source_match": "Function equality is equivalent to equality at every position; no approximation or almost-everywhere interpretation replaces the source equalities.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "Exists",
      "interpretation": "Existential quantification over an element satisfying a proposition.",
      "effect_on_target": "Quantifies one vector value at the origin for each fixed initialState and pair of states.",
      "source_match": "Expresses freedom at the point omitted from the source branches; the witness can be initialState 0.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "Fin",
      "interpretation": "The standard finite index type with m elements when applied to m.",

      "source_match": "Matches the chapter's real m-component state convention.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "Iff",
      "interpretation": "Logical equivalence, requiring both implications.",
      "effect_on_target": "Characterizes precisely which initial functions satisfy the branch predicate.",
      "source_match": "Gives an equivalent representation of the source prescription rather than asserting that arbitrary initial functions satisfy it.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "Nat",
      "interpretation": "The standard natural-number type including zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Indexes the number of real state components without imposing a positive-dimension premise.",
      "source_match": "Covers every positive component count in the source and harmlessly extends the branch characterization to the empty vector.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "Real",
      "interpretation": "Mathlib's real-number type at the declared external semantic frontier.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies both spatial coordinates and vector components.",
      "source_match": "Matches the real spatial domain and real state components introduced on printed page 1.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "LT.lt",
      "interpretation": "Projects the strict-order relation from the supplied LT instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Uses Real.instLT for the negative and positive spatial tests.",
      "source_match": "Preserves the strict inequalities in (1.11).",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "interpretation": "Projects the value assigned to a numeral by its OfNat instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the numeral zero through the real zero instance.",
      "source_match": "The branch boundary is the source's real spatial origin.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "Real.decidableLT",
      "interpretation": "Provides a Decidable instance for strict comparison of two reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the conditional definition in D002 without adding a hypothesis on the data.",
      "source_match": "Introduces no approximation or restriction on the source's real coordinates.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "Real.instLT",
      "interpretation": "Installs the real strict-order relation as the LT Real instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the two half-lines used by D002 and D003.",
      "source_match": "Matches the ordinary real ordering in x < 0 and x > 0.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "Real.instZero",
      "interpretation": "Installs real zero as the Zero Real instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the spatial interface used in both definitions.",
      "source_match": "Matches the source's chosen interface x = 0.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "interpretation": "Builds the numeral-zero interpretation from the supplied Zero instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects the literal 0 in branch tests to real zero.",
      "source_match": "Adds no offset or alternative boundary convention.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "ite",
      "interpretation": "Selects its first value when the proposition holds and its second value otherwise, by cases on Decidable.",
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the nested three-case initial function in D002.",
      "source_match": "Preserves both source branches; the remaining zero case is existentially unrestricted.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "And",
      "interpretation": "Logical conjunction requiring both propositions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires both the negative-side and positive-side equalities.",
      "source_match": "Neither branch of (1.11) is omitted or made optional.",
      "status": "pass"
    }
  ],
  "semantic_checklist": [
    {
      "id": "C01",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Attached raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2.1 displays (1.11). Attached page 23 supplies the real vector state convention; page 28 continues the linear/nonlinear discussion.",
      "lean_evidence": "The proof-free header and both elaborated types give the same initial-data characterization.",
      "reasoning": "The selected claim is the initial-data prescription, not the neighboring discussion of solution structure. Source identification and hashes are supplied provenance; I did not independently recompute them."
    },
    {
      "id": "C02",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Printed page 1 specifies q : R × R → R^m; (1.11) concerns q(x,0) and two fixed states.",
      "lean_evidence": "The binders are m : Nat, initialState : Real → Fin m → Real, and leftState rightState : Fin m → Real.",
      "reasoning": "The initial-time slice is represented by a function of position alone, with the intended vector-valued codomain."
    },
    {
      "id": "C03",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) prescribes constant states at every negative and positive position while omitting zero.",
      "lean_evidence": "D003 universally quantifies each real x; the target places Exists valueAtOrigin inside the binders for the whole initial function and states.",
      "reasoning": "One origin value belongs to each initial function. There is no position-dependent choice of left or right state or globally fixed origin value."
    },
    {
      "id": "C04",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The opening paragraph distinguishes the hyperbolic equation from its special initial data. The displayed formula has no regularity, neighboring-cell, or distinct-state hypothesis.",

      "reasoning": "No such premise is needed to characterize the selected data prescription. The prose's jump description does not require adding an inequality absent from the selected equation."
    },
    {
      "id": "C05",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) contains a negative-side left-state equality and a positive-side right-state equality at time zero.",
      "lean_evidence": "D003 contains both equalities; D002 and the existential provide their total-function characterization.",
      "reasoning": "Both prescribed cases are represented, and no positive-time condition is claimed."
    },
    {
      "id": "C06",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The source uses exact equality and strict real comparisons for a piecewise-constant prescription.",

      "reasoning": "Every supplied dependency has been interpreted, including the complete local definition bodies and the declared external semantic frontier."
    },
    {
      "id": "C07",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Both branches of (1.11) use equality and strict inequalities.",
      "lean_evidence": "D003 uses And, Eq, x < 0, and 0 < x; the target uses Iff with existential function equality.",
      "reasoning": "The equivalence expresses exactly the same admissible data, with no weakening to inequalities or almost-everywhere equality."
    },
    {
      "id": "C08",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "q(x,0), q_l, and q_r have distinct roles; the subsequent cell averages are an illustrative choice of states.",
      "lean_evidence": "initialState, leftState, rightState, and valueAtOrigin are separate objects, and no cell averages appear.",
      "reasoning": "The initial trace and fixed side states retain their roles. The origin witness is an unconstrained completion, not a third prescribed source state."
    },
    {
      "id": "C09",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) fixes spatial interface zero and initial time zero.",
      "lean_evidence": "D002 and D003 compare real positions with zero; initialState represents the time-zero slice.",
      "reasoning": "No interface shift, coefficient, index offset, or time dependence is introduced."
    },
    {
      "id": "C10",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The chapter allows real vector states and discusses both linear and nonlinear Riemann problems.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target covers arbitrary Fin m → Real states and imposes no linear-system structure; m may also be zero.",
      "reasoning": "All intended system dimensions are covered. The empty-vector case is a harmless degenerate extension of this logical characterization, not a restriction or a substantive strengthening of the source prescription."
    },
    {
      "id": "C11",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) omits x = 0 and contains no explicit q_l ≠ q_r requirement.",
      "lean_evidence": "D003 imposes no condition at zero; D002's valueAtOrigin is existentially quantified; equal side states are allowed.",
      "reasoning": "For any initial function satisfying the two branches, choose valueAtOrigin = initialState 0. No interface value or genuine-discontinuity condition is silently imposed."
    },
    {
      "id": "C12",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The two open half-lines admit independent constant states.",
      "lean_evidence": "For m = 1, choose leftState = 0, rightState = 1, and any origin state; D002 constructs a satisfying initial function.",
      "reasoning": "The admissible class is nonempty with distinct states. A function violating either side condition fails both representations, so the characterization does not make arbitrary data admissible."
    },
    {
      "id": "N01",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "The finite-volume application follows (1.11), but the selected equation itself prescribes initial data.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target contains a predicate and its piecewise-function representation, without an update rule.",
      "reasoning": "No algorithm, recurrence, or discretization is part of the selected claim."
    },
    {
      "id": "N02",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Printed page 1 identifies m real components; (1.11) equates whole states.",
      "lean_evidence": "States are Fin m → Real and are compared using Eq.",
      "reasoning": "Vector equality preserves equality of every component. No norm or metric convention is involved."
    },
    {
      "id": "N03",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) contains no error or stability assertion.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target contains only exact data equalities and logical equivalence.",
      "reasoning": "There is no numerical error or stability notion to compare."
    },
    {
      "id": "N04",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) gives an exact initial-data prescription; choosing states from neighboring cell averages is a subsequent application.",
      "lean_evidence": "The side states and initial function are arbitrary exact real-valued objects, with no rounding or approximation.",
      "reasoning": "The constructed function represents the same exact initial data and does not conflate it with computed numerical values."
    },
    {
      "id": "N05",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "(1.11) has no limit, remainder, or asymptotic qualification.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target is an exact equivalence without asymptotic operators.",
      "reasoning": "No asymptotic semantics are present in the selected claim."
    },
    {
      "id": "N06",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Section 1.2.1 distinguishes the data from the hyperbolic equation and subsequently discusses Riemann solutions.",
      "lean_evidence": "Exists quantifies only a vector value at the origin; no time-dependent solution is quantified.",
      "reasoning": "The witness completes an already given total initial function. It does not assert PDE existence, uniqueness, regularity, or well-posedness."
    }
  ],
  "implications": {
    "lean_implies_source": {
      "verdict": "yes",
      "reasoning": "As a characterization of admissible initial data, the existential representation yields initialState x = leftState for x < 0 and initialState x = rightState for x > 0 by the two conditional branches. Identifying initialState x with q(x,0) recovers precisely (1.11). The theorem does not assert that every arbitrary initialState satisfies this prescription."
    },
    "source_implies_lean": {
      "verdict": "yes",
      "reasoning": "Given a total initial trace satisfying (1.11), choose valueAtOrigin = initialState 0. For negative and positive x, the source branch equalities give agreement with riemannData; at zero the chosen witness gives agreement. Real-order trichotomy and function extensionality yield equality of functions. Conversely, that equality yields the source branches, establishing the stated characterization without an additional source condition."
    }
  },
  "classification": "faithful-equivalent",
  "accepted": true,
  "requires_adjudication": false,
  "findings": [],
  "rationale": "The attached primary-source images show exactly two strict half-line prescriptions at time zero, with no value assigned at the interface. The Lean proposition faithfully characterizes this class of initial traces through a total piecewise function with an existentially free origin value. It retains real vector states, both branch orientations, and pointwise equality, while making no evolution or solvability claim. All 17 dependencies and all 18 configured checks are accounted for; no unresolved semantic issue remains."
}
